subject: dog
readings: head at -x (nose points left in XY panel): XY panel is the profile view, ZY panel is the front/rear view, XZ panel is the top view
nose (2,9), skull/neck junction (10,5): head length ~5, extends forward and slightly downward from the skull
withers/neck junction (16,6) vs skull (10,5): neck length ~4, rises slightly and points forward to the head
withers (16,6), hip/croup (20,8): back length ~8, slopes gently down toward the hindquarters (larger screen-y = lower on the back)
hip (20,8), tail tip (17,1): tail curls forward and upward over the back, length ~6
shoulder (16,6, treated as withers) to elbow (15,14): front upper-leg length ~6, nearly straight down
elbow (15,14) to paw (16,22): front lower-leg length ~7, straight down to ground line y=22
hip (20,8) to knee (20,16): rear thigh length ~6, straight down
knee (20,16) to hock (22,18): lower rear-leg length ~4, down and slightly forward
hock (22,18) to paw (22,22): rear paw segment length ~3, straight down, matches ground line y=22 seen for front paws too

ZY panel: front-leg stance spans z=8 (animal-left) to z=16 (animal-right) around a body centerline of z=12, giving the lateral splay used for left/right leg directions; rear legs read a similar splay lower in the same panel
notes: Head/neck split inferred at the visible narrowing behind the ears (skull vs neck) in the XY panel. Front leg was split into two segments (shoulder-elbow, elbow-paw) since the profile shows a fairly straight limb with one visible bend at the elbow. Rear leg was split into three segments (thigh, lower-leg to hock, hock to paw) because the profile clearly shows the characteristic canine hock bend partway down the limb. Tail is encoded as a single curved-direction segment approximating its up-and-forward curl over the back rather than multiple segments, since only base and tip are clearly distinguishable in the render. Left/right leg lateral (z) offsets are taken from the ZY (front) panel's leg stance spread around the body centerline; sign convention: +z = animal's right side, -z = animal's left side. Ears, eyes, and other head details are sub-flap features and were not given separate leaves per the protocol. Vertical directions were sign-flipped from the screen's downward-increasing y grid so that all descending limbs have negative dy, verified on the front leg (shoulder to paw goes from y=6 to y=22 on screen, i.e. down, giving negative world dy).
